hook.text: Can’t find what you’re looking for?

summary.tone: Calm, minimal and confident: off-white canvas, black kinetic type, real-looking product UI, light music bed with no voice-over.

signature_moments.description: Six integration icons fly in with motion blur and a grey highlight scans across them on the beat, cut into tight crops that keep the scan rhythm.
signature_moments.why_premium: Shows the whole integration story in seconds without words, and the beat-locked scan plus hard crops give energy from very few elements.

signature_moments.description: The icon row collapses into a single Notion logo, then the 'Introducing Notion AI connectors' headline slides left as the Slack connect modal slides in and a cursor ticks channels.
signature_moments.why_premium: One continuous re-layout carries the viewer from idea to product with no cut, so the headline and the UI read as one argument.

signature_moments.description: A fast blurred push from the Projects board into the AI panel, where a typed question returns a cited answer drawing on a Slack thread.
signature_moments.why_premium: The payoff is shown, not told: the cited Slack source proves the connector claim inside a believable product moment.

hook.evidence: Recognisable app icons in motion grab attention instantly and lead into a relatable question headline; it takes ~7s before any text appears, which is slow for a 32s piece.

clarity.evidence: One idea per beat: problem question, product name, connect step, benefit line, demo answer with sources, CTA. Short headlines and real UI make the value obvious.

ui_showcase.evidence: Two crisp product moments (Slack channel connect modal, AI chat with cited answer) with a scripted cursor; small UI text and the brief board view are hard to read at 2 fps scale.

motion_polish.evidence: Consistent per-word fade reveals, a motion-blurred icon entrance, icon-to-logo merge, headline/modal re-layout and a blurred camera push; motion is clean but conservative and reuses one text effect throughout.

sound_design.evidence: Judged from anchors only: a ~97.5 BPM music bed at -23.5 LUFS integrated, and just three detected events, all in s005 (swoosh_reverse at 24.8s near the typing/panel open, a music event at 28.1s, swoosh_reverse at 29.8s before the logo). The icon scan visually follows the beat grid. Competent and quiet, not distinctive.

vo_script_quality.evidence: No voice-over: the anchors transcript has no words; the script is carried entirely by on-screen text.

brand_consistency.evidence: Notion's off-white canvas, black sans headlines, genuine Notion UI and a closing cube-logo lockup stay consistent from first to last frame.

works_muted.evidence: No voice-over; every message is on-screen text or visible UI, so the video reads fully with sound off.

overall.evidence: A tight, on-brand 32s launch teaser with a clear problem-product-proof-CTA arc and polished but restrained motion; audio and the slow opening keep it short of best-in-class.

localization_friendliness.notes: No voice-over, so no dubbing is needed, but all headlines are animated per word and the UI (channel names, typed question, AI answer, board cards) is baked in English; localising means re-rendering the headline animations and re-capturing or rebuilding the UI.

annotation.typography: Same bold/semibold neo-grotesque sans as earlier shots (Inter or Notion's own sans, low confidence), sentence case, slightly tight tracking, centered two-line and one-line headlines; each word fades in from light grey to near-black in sequence. UI uses small regular-weight sans; the user question sits in a grey pill bubble, the answer in regular weight with a small blue citation badge. Final lockup is the Notion wordmark in bold sans beside the cube logo.
annotation.what_happens: "Access all your company’s knowledge" finishes building word by word and holds; it clears and "without leaving Notion" builds the same way. At ~22s a full Notion Projects kanban board appears as a shadowed window, then the camera pushes in fast with motion blur onto the board's right side; the cursor moves to the bottom-right AI button and the Notion AI chat panel opens over the board. The question "What is the mobile team working on this week?" types into the input, is sent and rises into a grey bubble; an answer appears below with a citation badge, "1 source found", a page and a Slack thread source; the cursor hovers the citation badge. The frame clears to blank, "Try it now" builds word by word, then the Notion cube logo appears alone and the "Notion" wordmark slides in beside it. Board card details and the badge number are too small to read reliably.
annotation.build_rebuild: Reuse the per-word opacity headline component for two headlines, then show a shadowed kanban window, scale it ~2.5x toward its bottom-right with a short motion blur, open a chat panel, type the question character by character (~25 chars/s), move it into a right-aligned bubble and fade in a two-line answer plus a source list, then clear to a 'Try it now' headline and a logo-then-wordmark lockup.

pattern.description: Six integration app icons enter one after another left to right, each rising from slightly below while blurred and transparent and settling sharp into a row; once the last icon lands, a soft rounded tray fades in behind them to group the row as one dock.
pattern.why_premium: The left-to-right blur-and-rise stagger reads as a quick, ordered roll call of connectors, and adding the tray only after the last icon lands turns six loose logos into one product surface without a second cut.

build_hint.gsap: tl.fromTo('.app-icon', {y: 40, opacity: 0, filter: 'blur(10px)'}, {y: 0, opacity: 1, filter: 'blur(0px)', duration: 0.35, ease: 'power3.out', stagger: 0.12}).fromTo('.tray', {opacity: 0}, {opacity: 1, duration: 0.3, ease: 'power2.out'}, '-=0.05')
build_hint.remotion: For icon i: const p = spring({frame: frame - i*4, fps, config: {damping: 30, stiffness: 180, mass: 1}}) (no overshoot); translateY = interpolate(p, [0,1], [40,0]); opacity = p; blur = interpolate(p, [0,1], [10,0]). Tray opacity = interpolate(frame, [26, 35], [0, 1], {easing: Easing.out(Easing.quad), extrapolateLeft: 'clamp', extrapolateRight: 'clamp'}).

events.notes: Icons seem to enter from slightly below and to the right of their slots; the direction is approximate from blurred frames. camera.move is none, so the raw scale/pan_y sums reflect the icons and tray arriving, not a camera move. No SFX candidates even though the spectrogram shows music.

pattern.description: Inside a static connector-logo tray, individual app tiles flash to a darkened grey state for one or two frames, one tile at a time (Jira, then GitHub), then snap back to white.
pattern.why_premium: The flashes land on music transients in the stem, so a static logo row gets a rhythmic pulse without any layout movement, keeping the tray readable while signalling each integration in turn.

build_hint.gsap: Static tray; for each tile in order, a timeline `.set(tile, {filter: 'brightness(0.55) saturate(0)'})` at the beat time followed by `.set(tile, {filter: 'none'}, '+=0.067')` (step, no tween). Place tiles on beat timestamps rather than a fixed stagger.
build_hint.remotion: Per tile, compute `const on = frame >= beatFrame && frame < beatFrame + 2;` and apply `filter: on ? 'brightness(0.55) grayscale(1)' : 'none'` with no interpolation; beatFrame comes from the music beat list per tile.

events.notes: b01 is a union box covering both the Jira and GitHub tiles, which flash at different frames (f110 Jira, f120 GitHub); recorded as one element to avoid inventing a box. pattern.description: Centered two-line question builds word by word in sync with narration: each new word fades in light grey and darkens to near-black while the centered lines re-center and wrap as words are added.
pattern.why_premium: Word-paced reveal locks the text to the voice, and the grey-to-black settle gives each word a soft landing instead of a hard pop; the live re-centering keeps the composition balanced at every frame.

build_hint.gsap: Split headline into words; tl.fromTo(words, {opacity: 0, color: '#9a9a9a'}, {opacity: 1, color: '#111', duration: 0.3, ease: 'power2.out', stagger: 0.17}); animate the line container's x/y with Flip (or a short power2.inOut tween) so the centered block re-centers as each word lands.
build_hint.remotion: Per word i: start = i*5 frames at 30fps; opacity = interpolate(frame-start, [0, 4], [0, 1]); color = interpolateColors(frame-start, [0, 9], ['#9a9a9a', '#111']); recompute centered layout from visible words and smooth its offset with spring({damping: 200}) (no overshoot).

events.notes: Word order of reveal: Can't, find, what, you're, looking, for?. Earlier words drift slightly as the centered layout reflows (camera.move none; scale 1.03 reflects reflow, not a camera move). No SFX candidates.

pattern.description: After a hard cut from the question card, a centered row of six app-tile icons (Google Drive, Slack, Notion, Jira, GitHub, Salesforce) collapses inward; the other tiles slide under the Notion tile and disappear, leaving the Notion logo alone at center.
pattern.why_premium: One converging move tells the story (all your tools fold into Notion) with no copy; the Notion tile is layered on top so the others visibly tuck behind it, and the shared ease makes the stack resolve as a single gesture.

build_hint.gsap: Row of tiles with Notion at highest z-index; tl.to(otherTiles, {x: (i, el) => centerX - el.centerX, duration: 0.5, ease: 'power3.inOut', stagger: {from: 'edges', each: 0.02}}).to(otherTiles, {opacity: 0, duration: 0.15}, '-=0.15') while notionTile tweens x to center with the same ease.
build_hint.remotion: For each tile, progress = interpolate(frame, [0, 15], [0, 1], {easing: Easing.inOut(Easing.cubic)}); translateX = (centerX - tileX) * progress; opacity drops to 0 over the last 4 frames for non-Notion tiles; Notion tile rendered last (on top) and translated to center.

events.notes: Question text exits via a hard cut at the start of the burst (energy spike at frame ~304), not animated; not listed as an element. Outer vs inner icon grouping onto b01/b02 is approximate since the icons end hidden behind the Notion tile; camera.move none, scale 0.69 reflects content collapsing, not a zoom. No SFX candidates.

pattern.description: A virtual camera pushes in fast (about 1.8x) from the full Notion Projects kanban board to a close crop of the middle columns, drifting toward the lower right. Heavy motion blur during travel resolves to sharp cards, and the cursor is waiting in the empty column.
pattern.why_premium: A fast eased push with real motion blur pulls attention from overview to detail in about 0.6 s without a cut, so the viewer keeps spatial context, and the sharp settle makes the UI feel tangible.

build_hint.gsap: Animate a camera wrapper: gsap.fromTo('.board', {scale: 1, x: 0, y: 0, filter: 'blur(0px)'}, {scale: 1.78, xPercent: -25, yPercent: -28, duration: 0.6, ease: 'power3.inOut'}), with a parallel blur tween to blur(6px) at the midpoint and back to 0 (yoyo). Fade the cursor in at the end (opacity 0->1, 0.15s).
build_hint.remotion: const p = interpolate(frame, [0, 18], [0, 1], {easing: Easing.bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1), extrapolateRight: 'clamp'}); transform: scale(1 + 0.78*p) translate(...); motion blur via @remotion/motion-blur or filter blur(sin(p*PI)*6px). Could also use spring({damping: 200}) with no overshoot.

events.notes: The camera verdict is push_in (scale 1.78, pan up-left in content coordinates). The individual cards (b03-b20) only move with the camera, so they are not listed separately. The cursor may have been hidden by blur rather than faded in; it is clearly visible only at f695. Energy tails off after f687 with a slight settle drift.

pattern.description: The Notion AI chat panel snaps open over the Projects board with its input already focused (blue ring). The board behind it fades to the off-white background, then the question types in character by character ('W' ... 'What is the m').
pattern.why_premium: Fading the board out leaves the AI panel as the only subject, and the realistic char-by-char typing shows the real product interaction instead of a mockup, building anticipation for the answer.

build_hint.gsap: tl.set('.ai-panel', {autoAlpha: 1}) at the cut; tl.to('.board', {opacity: 0, duration: 0.45, ease: 'power2.inOut'}, '<+0.1'); then type the prompt with a TextPlugin or a char-split stagger: tl.from(chars, {opacity: 0, duration: 0.01, stagger: 0.035, ease: 'none'}, '<+0.2').

events.notes: The panel appears in one step at f715 (energy spike) and has no candidate box, hence the manual_box. b01 also includes the panel area, but here it stands for the board fading behind it. Board cards b03-b20 fade with the board and are not listed separately. The cursor jumps between f705 and f715 but has no candidate box; it is left out. Typing continues past the event end.

pattern.description: The send step of the prompt: the typed question disappears from the focused input in one frame, and the same text appears as a right-aligned grey chat bubble above the 'Find in' chip, fading in with a small upward drift. At the end of the burst a faint response row begins to ghost in below it.
pattern.why_premium: Clearing the input and fading the bubble in quickly reads as an instant 'sent' without a literal button press, and the soft rise of the bubble plus the hint of a coming answer keeps momentum into the AI response.

build_hint.gsap: tl.set('.input-text', {textContent: ''}); tl.fromTo('.user-bubble', {opacity: 0, y: 8}, {opacity: 1, y: 0, duration: 0.22, ease: 'power2.out'}, '<'); tl.fromTo('.answer-ghost', {opacity: 0}, {opacity: 0.15, duration: 0.3, ease: 'power1.out'}, '+=0.25').
build_hint.remotion: Input text hidden from frame 0. Bubble: const p = spring({frame, fps, config: {damping: 200, stiffness: 180}}); opacity = p, translateY = interpolate(p, [0,1], [8,0]). Ghost row opacity = interpolate(frame, [22, 30], [0, 0.15], {extrapolateLeft: 'clamp', extrapolateRight: 'clamp'}).

events.notes: The pattern is the send step of prompt_type_on (it could also be seen as the start of ai_answer_stream). The bubble's small rise is inferred from where it sits relative to the 'Find in' chip across the filmstrip. The faint row at the end of the burst (energy spike at f789) is very low contrast; its box and role are guesses.

pattern.description: With the AI answer already on screen, the cursor glides diagonally from near the send button at the bottom right up to the blue Slack citation chip '2' after 'outage', showing motion blur on the way, and comes to rest on the chip, ready to open the source.
pattern.why_premium: One smooth eased cursor path with motion blur leads the eye straight to the citation that proves the connector works (a Slack source), with no jitter or detour, like a scripted, retimed screen recording.

build_hint.gsap: gsap.fromTo('.cursor', {x: 135, y: 300}, {x: 0, y: 0, duration: 0.5, ease: 'power2.inOut'}) along a straight diagonal (or motionPath with a slight curve). Optional directional blur via filter during travel.
build_hint.remotion: const p = interpolate(frame, [0, 15], [0, 1], {easing: Easing.bezier(0.45, 0, 0.55, 1), extrapolateRight: 'clamp'}); left = interpolate(p, [0,1], [955, 820]); top = interpolate(p, [0,1], [655, 360]). Spring({damping: 200}) with no overshoot also works.

events.notes: Only the cursor moves. b03 marks its start area and b01 the union of its path; b02 is the settled position. The Slack chip shows no visible hover change by f842.

pattern.description: The CTA headline 'Try it now' builds word by word: 'it' then 'now' fade in from light grey to near-black in place, staggered, after 'Try' is already set.
pattern.why_premium: Pure opacity/tone reveal with a tight per-word stagger keeps the layout fixed and lets the reading rhythm match the voice; no gimmicky motion on a calm off-white canvas.

build_hint.gsap: Split headline into words; gsap.fromTo(words, {opacity: 0}, {opacity: 1, duration: 0.3, ease: 'power2.out', stagger: 0.12}) with 'Try' already visible; optionally tween color from #9a9a9a to #111 alongside.
build_hint.remotion: Per word i: opacity = interpolate(frame - i*4, [0, 9], [0, 1], {easing: Easing.out(Easing.quad), extrapolateLeft: 'clamp', extrapolateRight: 'clamp'}); no spring needed, ease-out fade.

events.notes: Filmstrip is a zoomed crop; 'now' looks positionally static so no slide is reported. Words appear grey mid-fade, which may be opacity alone over the light background rather than a true colour shift.

pattern.description: End-card lockup: the centred cube logomark glides left to make room while the 'Notion' wordmark fades in from grey to black beside it, resolving into the horizontal lockup.
pattern.why_premium: The mark moves only as far as the lockup needs, and the wordmark fades in during that move, so the logo settles in one smooth step with no bounce or extra decoration.

build_hint.gsap: Start with the mark centred (x offset = +wordmarkWidth/2) and wordmark opacity 0. tl.to(mark, {x: 0, duration: 0.45, ease: 'power3.inOut'}).fromTo(wordmark, {opacity: 0, x: -20}, {opacity: 1, x: 0, duration: 0.35, ease: 'power2.out'}, '-=0.3').
build_hint.remotion: const p = interpolate(frame, [0, 14], [0, 1], {easing: Easing.inOut(Easing.cubic), extrapolateRight: 'clamp'}); mark translateX = (1 - p) * wordmarkWidth / 2; wordmark opacity = interpolate(frame, [5, 16], [0, 1], {easing: Easing.out(Easing.quad), extrapolateLeft: 'clamp', extrapolateRight: 'clamp'}). Ease, not spring.

events.notes: Filmstrip panels are zoomed crops of different extents, so the exact mark travel and whether the wordmark also slides is uncertain; camera verdict is none, so the pan/scale sums reflect the lockup reflow, not a camera move.
